citation: MacLachlan et al. Micron: an actively stabilized handheld tool for microsurgery. IEEE Transactions on Robotics.
access: Author full text; selected relevant sections
locator: Sections II-N and III-IV; bandwidth discussion p12
finding: Actively moving a handheld tool tip is feasible; reported closed-loop bandwidth 84-123 Hz.
limitation: External optical reference and microsurgical tasks do not establish loaded handwriting performance.
decision: Use as control precedent, not a transferable pen efficacy percentage.

citation: Becker, MacLachlan and Riviere. State Estimation and Feedforward Tremor Suppression for a Handheld Micromanipulator with a Kalman Filter. IROS.
access: Author full text; selected relevant sections
finding: Feedback plus prediction reduced RMS error from 7.9 to 3.4 micrometres in the reported hold-still comparison.
limitation: Improvement is relative to feedback-only Micron, not a conventional pen or handwriting population.
decision: Predict through measured latency; benchmark against feedback-only control.

citation: Tironi et al. A smart pen prototype with adaptive algorithms for stabilizing handwriting tremor signals in Parkinson's disease. Scientific Reports 15:28659.
access: Publisher full text; methods, results and conclusion
locator: Materials and methods; real-time performance; data availability
finding: Adaptive filters and embedded execution were tested; no human participants in device validation.
limitation: Signal MSE does not establish ink improvement. Dataset description mentions both JPEG images and recorded time series; exact signal provenance requires checking.
decision: Use as an algorithm baseline only; require physical ink and independent motion outcomes.

citation: Bain et al. Primary writing tremor. Brain 118:1461-1472.
access: PubMed abstract
finding: Writing-tremor frequencies 4.1-7.3 Hz overlapped normal writing oscillations of 4.0-7.7 Hz.
limitation: Small task-specific cohort; not a universal frequency distribution.
decision: A frequency threshold cannot by itself distinguish intent from tremor.

citation: Elble et al. Quantification of essential tremor in writing and drawing. Movement Disorders 11:70-78.
access: PubMed abstract
finding: Wrist and writing tremor measures were weakly correlated; very severe cases could lose tablet contact.
limitation: Task- and device-specific; missing pen contact can bias recorded severity.
decision: Measure actual ink and pen-up time, not only wrist acceleration.

citation: Latimer et al. The effects of auditory cues and weighted pens on handwriting in individuals with Parkinson's disease. Journal of Hand Therapy 37:144-152.
access: Indexed PubMed abstract; subsequent direct access challenged
locator: Abstract; 8 participants; repeated cursive l task
finding: The weighted pen increased spatial and timing variability in this small novice-user sample.
limitation: Not a trial of an actively controlled mass; short task and small sample.
decision: Always compare active tail with the same mass locked and with no tail.

citation: Nackaerts et al. Relearning of Writing Skills in Parkinson's Disease After Intensive Amplitude Training. Movement Disorders 31:1209-1216.
access: Indexed PubMed abstract; full text not reviewed
locator: Abstract; 38 people; 6 weeks training and retention assessment
finding: Provides a controlled framework for testing handwriting amplitude training.
limitation: Training evidence does not validate an automatic mechanical pen or immediate tremor suppression.
decision: Evaluate micrographia cueing and unassisted retention separately.

citation: Schomaker and Plamondon. The relation between pen force and pen-point kinematics in handwriting. Biological Cybernetics 63:277-289.
access: Author full text; methods and tables
finding: Axial pen force and point kinematics are distinct measurements with substantial task and writer variation.
limitation: Older restricted-posture setup; axial force must not be relabelled paper-normal force.
decision: Measure refill force and grip/paper load separately in the new fixture.

citation: Fu and Cavusoglu. Human-arm-and-hand-dynamic model with variability analyses for a stylus-based haptic interface. IEEE TSMC-B 42:1633-1644.
access: Citation identified in primary index; full text not retrieved in this review
locator: Publication identity; existing repository HAP-26 is the secondary parameter pointer
finding: Relevant precedent for identifying grip and arm dynamics.
limitation: Numerical parameters in the existing ledger were not independently reverified; posture and contact transfer remain unknown.
decision: Do not reuse its parameter values as measured writing-hand impedance.

citation: Langerak et al. Dynamic Drawing Guidance via Electromagnetic Haptic Feedback.
evidence: Physical prototype and initial human experiment
access: Author full text; hardware and evaluation sections
finding: Under-table electromagnet provides externally grounded guidance; reported lateral force up to 488 mN and dispersion 2.8 +/- 0.8 mm.
limitation: Large external apparatus, task-specific dispersion; not submillimetre pen-tip accuracy or autonomous spelling.
decision: A grounded accessory is credible for sustained guidance; remeasure accuracy at letter scale.

citation: Zenner and Krueger. Shifty: A Weight-Shifting Dynamic Passive Haptic Proxy. IEEE TVCG 23:1285-1294.
access: Author-institution abstract; PDF retrieval failed
finding: Redistributing weight can change perceived object properties.
limitation: Perceived weight/direction is not demonstrated writing-path control.
decision: Separate weight-balance cues from guaranteed steering force.

citation: HapticWhirl, a Flywheel-Gimbal Handheld Haptic Controller for Exploring Multimodal Haptic Feedback. Sensors 24:935.
access: Indexed publisher full-text hardware section; direct retrieval failed
finding: A 95 mm flywheel and 720 g complete device demonstrate torque-feedback hardware at a much larger scale.
limitation: Not a tremor-treatment trial or compact pen; do not extrapolate miniaturization from perception alone.
decision: Explicitly calculate rotor momentum, gimbal volume and containment.

citation: Bluteau et al. Haptic Guidance Improves the Visuo-Manual Tracking of Trajectories. PLOS ONE 3:e1775.
access: Publisher full text; methods and discussion
finding: Force and position guidance can affect different aspects of tracking and fluency.
limitation: Not proof of dyslexia spelling support or durable benefit from this pen.
decision: Test assistance while on separately from later unassisted learning.

citation: Luethi, Fender and Holz. DeltaPen: A Device with Integrated High-Precision Translation and Rotation Sensing on Passive Surfaces. UIST.
access: Author full text; hardware and evaluation sections
finding: Dual optical flow at 1 kHz; translation magnitude MAE 68.3 micrometres per 10 ms window, median 23.6 micrometres.
limitation: Evaluation on Wacom surface; USB-powered; no numeric end-to-end latency proof for our moving-nib paper geometry.
decision: Use for a sensing demonstrator; do not substitute 3 micrometres of white noise for its measured error.

citation: Fraunhofer IIS. Online Handwriting Recognition from Sensor-Enhanced Pens: OnHW datasets and publications.
access: Primary project page; benchmark descriptions
locator: Dataset and publications sections; updated page accessed 2026
finding: Provides sensor-pen recognition datasets and writer-dependent/independent benchmarks.
limitation: Not paired intention/tremor ground truth, nor evidence for a high-bandwidth closed-loop pen.
decision: Use to benchmark recognition and test writer-disjoint generalization, subject to licence.

citation: Graves et al. Connectionist Temporal Classification: Labelling Unsegmented Sequence Data with Recurrent Neural Networks. ICML.
access: Author full text; method
finding: CTC trains sequence labels without manual frame alignment.
limitation: CTC does not make a bidirectional encoder causal or recover the writer's hidden intent.
decision: Use a causal recognizer for streaming, with explicit endpointing and latency.

citation: Graves. Generating Sequences With Recurrent Neural Networks.
access: Abstract only
finding: Demonstrates sequence generation and text-conditioned handwriting synthesis.
limitation: Generated strokes do not establish mechanical reachability or correct user intent.
decision: Separate style generation from a constrained physical motion planner.

citation: Guo et al. On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks. ICML / PMLR 70:1321-1330.
access: Primary proceedings abstract and linked paper
finding: High classification confidence can be miscalibrated; temperature scaling is a useful baseline.
limitation: Calibration on one distribution does not guarantee reliability under handwriting or language shift.
decision: Validate selective prediction and abstention on held-out writers and devices.

citation: Li et al. Enhancing IMU-Based Online Handwriting Recognition via Contrastive Learning with Zero Inference Overhead.
access: Abstract only
finding: Training-time auxiliary contrastive learning is a candidate for better writer-independent recognition without extra deployed branches.
limitation: Preprint and abstract-level review; no closed-loop physical-control evidence.
decision: Candidate benchmark extension, not a reason to replace a measured control baseline.

citation: How do technologies meet the needs of the writer with dyslexia? An examination of functions scaffolding the transcription and proofreading in text production. Dyslexia.
access: Indexed PubMed abstract; full text not retrieved
finding: Spelling aids may trade accuracy against time and attention; severe-difficulty performance remains unclear.
limitation: Feature analysis rather than validation of our hardware or all dyslexic writers.
decision: Measure workload, accepted suggestions, harmful edits and writing fluency.

citation: Rello et al. A Computer-Based Method to Improve the Spelling of Children with Dyslexia. ASSETS 2014; author preprint posted 2015.
access: Author abstract only
finding: Examines spelling exercises based on actual errors and switching games over an intervention.
limitation: Learning exercises do not validate automatic ink correction; full methods not assessed here.
decision: Personalized confusion data is useful; assess learning and assistance separately.

citation: Texas Instruments. TMAG5273 Low-Power Linear 3D Hall-Effect Sensor, datasheet SLYS045C.
access: Datasheet; relevant timing and noise tables
finding: 10 kSPS for three axes at 1x averaging; 0.4 kSPS at 32x; 1 MHz maximum I2C clock.
limitation: Conversion rate is not delivered loop bandwidth; noise depends on mode and position sensitivity.
decision: Budget bus time, filter delay and coil-field interference.

citation: Texas Instruments. DRV8214 2-A Brushed DC Motor Driver with Ripple Counting, Stall Detection, and Speed Regulation.
access: Datasheet; current-sense and bridge sections
locator: Electrical characteristics; current sense and bridge control
finding: Integrated current mirror and regulation have explicit ranges, error and blanking times.
limitation: Brushed-motor ripple counting does not measure voice-coil displacement; peak current is not thermal continuous capability.
decision: Validate signed current sensing, PWM modes and low-voltage headroom on a coil.

citation: STMicroelectronics. LSM6DSV16X 6-axis inertial measurement unit datasheet.
access: Datasheet and product overview; relevant sensor features
locator: Sensor architecture; operating-mode and filter sections
finding: Accelerometer and gyroscope provide local motion sensing with selectable modes and filters.
limitation: Embedded sensor fusion is not an absolute page-position measurement or clinical tremor discriminator.
decision: Timestamp acquisition, characterize delay, calibrate lever arm and bias.

citation: PI Ceramic. PL112-PL140 PICMA multilayer piezo bending actuators.
access: Datasheet; specification table and clamping notes
finding: PL128 nominal free displacement +/-450 micrometres and blocking force +/-0.55 N are endpoint specifications with tolerances.
limitation: Endpoints cannot be achieved simultaneously; custom widths and actual preload change performance.
decision: Evaluate the force-travel line, loaded resonance and driver energy before selecting a piezo.
